we have developed a technique to perform spatially resolved hyper‐polarized 3He q‐space imaging that allows the acquisition of a 3D dataset in a single breath hold.
we developed and tested a novel method to measure diffusion in the lung using hyperpolarized gas MRI.

we have developed a novel hyperpolarized 3He MR imaging technique for lung microstructure assessment in three dimensions, which has been tested in a healthy human and is now ready for application to lung disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of MRI in the diagnosis and monitoring of pulmonary disease.
the development and application of novel magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) techniques to study the human lung.
the design and development of new MR imaging techniques to measure lung function and structure.

the proposed technique has been shown to be feasible for hyperpolarized He‐3 MRI q‐space imaging in vivo, and the results are consistent with previous studies.
the authors have developed a method that can be used for 3D microstructure imaging of lung disease in a single breath-hold.
the authors have demonstrated a novel technique for the acquisition of hyperpolarized 3 He q‐space imaging data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that q‐space imaging can be performed on helium‐3 MR data with radial acquisition and highly constrained back‐projections.
we have developed a novel method for imaging the diffusion of hyperpolarized 3He in the lung.
we developed and tested a technique for measuring the diffusion distance in the lungs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have developed an imaging technique that can be used to evaluate the microstructure of the lungs in a single breath-hold, and that this technique can be used to measure the diffusion distance of helium-3 in a single breath hold, which is a measure of the size of the air spaces within the lungs.
it is possible to perform q‐space imaging of hyperpolarized gas in a breath‐held scan using an iterative reconstruction technique.
we were the first to demonstrate that it was possible to do q-space imaging of the lungs with hyperpolarized gas.
